content.text: Section 11 fully addresses the rule; no conflicting deletion or carve-out language exists elsewhere.

input.quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
input.rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position. Transition obligations are triggered "[u]pon expiry or termination for any reason" with no carve-out for Vendor termination for cause (11.1); Vendor must provide up to six months of transition assistance (11.1); Customer Data must be returned within thirty days in a "complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format" (11.2), and Vendor must securely delete remaining Customer Data and certify deletion in writing only after Customer confirms successful return (11.3). Two immaterial variances, both favourable to us, are noted rather than flagged: assistance is priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form rather than Vendor's then-current rates, and the thirty-day return clock runs from Customer's request rather than the termination date, leaving timing under our control. Sections 10 and 15 contain no conflicting deletion or data-retention mechanic, and 16.3 expressly leaves Customer Data governed by Sections 11 and 15. No redline required.
